issues.legal_issue: The improvement law may be applied to a municipal area while its committee is superseded, with the administrator exercising the committee’s power to oppose its application and the government appointing trustees during supersession.
material_facts: The municipal committee had been superseded when the government extended the improvement law to the municipal area and established a trust.
An administrator had been appointed with the powers and duties of the superseded committee.
The government appointed trustees while the committee remained superseded.
The rate-payers challenged the trust’s establishment.
issues.conclusion: The trust could validly be established while the committee was superseded; the administrator could exercise the committee’s power to oppose application of the law, and the government could appoint trustees during supersession.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 1(3) of the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922, the committee’s power to resolve against application of the Act could, while the committee was superseded, be exercised by the administrator under section 238 of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, which transferred all the committee’s powers and duties to the appointed persons. Section 4A of the 1922 Act provided for the government to fill the committee’s allotted trustee seats during supersession. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: municipal_committee_superseded and improvement_law_applied_to_area and administrator_exercised_committee_powers and government_appointed_trustees_during_supersession and trust_creation_challenged

predicates.municipal_committee_superseded: The municipal committee had been superseded when the improvement law was applied to its area.
predicates.improvement_law_applied_to_area: The government applied the improvement law to the municipal area.
predicates.administrator_exercised_committee_powers: An appointed administrator held and exercised the powers and duties of the superseded committee.
predicates.government_appointed_trustees_during_sup: The government appointed trustees while the committee remained superseded.
predicates.trust_creation_challenged: Rate-payers brought a proceeding challenging the establishment of the trust.

issues.definition: When a trust’s establishment is challenged after the improvement law has been applied to an area whose committee was superseded, the trust is validly established during supersession if an administrator held the committee’s powers and the government appointed trustees during that period.

issues.legal_issue: Once the improvement law has come into operation in a municipal area, reconstitution of the municipal committee does not require the law to be applied to the area again.
material_facts: The improvement law had been applied to the municipal area while its committee was superseded.
The municipal committee was later reconstituted and passed a resolution opposing the trust’s reconstitution.
Rate-payers challenged the government’s subsequent reconstitution of the trust.
issues.conclusion: The improvement law continued to apply after the municipal committee was reconstituted, and it did not need to be applied again.
issues.legal_principle: Section 1(3) of the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922, contains no provision under which the Act ceases to apply once it has come into operation, nor does it require reapplication after a municipal committee is reconstituted. The dissolution of a trust under section 103 does not itself terminate the Act’s application to the area. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: improvement_law_previously_applied and municipal_committee_later_reconstituted and committee_opposed_trust_reconstitution and challenge_to_trust_reconstitution

predicates.improvement_law_previously_applied: The government had already brought the improvement law into operation in the municipal area.
predicates.municipal_committee_later_reconstituted: The municipal committee was reconstituted after the law had come into operation.
predicates.committee_opposed_trust_reconstitution: The reconstituted committee passed a resolution opposing the trust’s reconstitution.
predicates.challenge_to_trust_reconstitution: Rate-payers brought a proceeding challenging the government’s reconstitution of the trust.

issues.definition: When a reconstituted committee opposes a trust’s reconstitution in a proceeding challenging that reconstitution, a law already in operation in the area continues to apply without being applied again.

issues.legal_issue: The government may create a new trust or reconstitute a dissolved trust under the statutory provisions governing the trust’s establishment and the continuing exercise of statutory powers.
material_facts: The trust had been dissolved by government notification under the improvement law.
The government later decided to reconstitute the trust and appointed a chairman.
issues.conclusion: The government had power to create a new trust or reconstitute the dissolved trust.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4 of the Punjab Town Improvement Act, 1922, provide for the establishment of a trust and the appointment of its trustees. Section 12 of the General Clauses (Punjab) Act, 1898, provides that a power conferred by a Punjab Act may be exercised from time to time as occasion requires. Read together, these provisions authorize the government to create a new trust or reconstitute a dissolved trust. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.trust_previously_dissolved: The government had dissolved the trust before the later attempt to constitute it again.
predicates.government_reconstituted_trust: The government took steps to constitute the trust again after its dissolution.
predicates.challenge_to_trust_reconstitution: Rate-payers brought a proceeding challenging the government’s reconstitution of the trust.

issues.definition: When a dissolved trust is reconstituted by the government and that action is challenged, the government may reconstitute the dissolved trust.
